blocks.text: Heart failure is a syndrome in which the heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs at normal filling pressures. Types: **heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)**, typically ejection fraction 40% or less, and **heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)**. Causes include coronary artery disease, hypertension, valve disease and cardiomyopathy. Reduced output causes fatigue and breathlessness; fluid backs up into the lungs (left-sided) or the body (right-sided).

rows: Slight limitation; comfortable at rest, ordinary activity causes symptoms
Marked limitation; less than ordinary activity causes symptoms

blocks.text: Breathlessness on exertion, orthopnoea (needs pillows to sleep), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (waking breathless), fatigue, ankle swelling, weight gain, reduced exercise tolerance, fine crackles at lung bases.

Daily weight trend (sudden gain of about 2 kg in 2 to 3 days suggests fluid retention [Ref – to verify]); pillows needed; swelling; recent medication changes; devices (pacemaker, ICD); fluid restriction; dizziness.

sections.title: D to E. Examination and measures

blocks.text: Vital signs, SpO2, weight, oedema (pitting), auscultation (crackles), jugular venous pressure (if trained), 6MWT, NYHA class, quality of life (Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire or Minnesota Living with Heart Failure) [Ref – to verify].

sections.title: G. RED FLAGS AND URGENT CONDITIONS

rows: Breathless at rest, pink frothy sputum, cannot lie flat
Resting HR or BP outside agreed limits

steps: **Stable (no decompensation in recent days, medications stable)?** Exercise training is recommended [Ref – to verify ESC guideline].
**Decompensated?** Medical management first; gentle mobility only as cleared.
**Device present?** Know the ICD threshold; keep HR at least about 10 to 20 beats below it [Ref – to verify].

sections.title: I to J. Exercise prescription (example, stable HFrEF)

rows: Start low: 40 to 50% of peak capacity or RPE 11 to 13; 10 to 20 min, increasing to 30 to 45 min; 3 to 5 days a week. Intervals helpful for very deconditioned patients
Low load, high repetition (for example 1 to 2 sets of 10 to 15 at RPE 11 to 13), avoid breath holding
Consider if inspiratory muscles are weak [Ref – to verify]
Daily weights, fluid and salt guidance as per the medical team, symptom monitoring, medication adherence, when to seek help

items: **Is exercise safe in heart failure?** In stable patients, supervised exercise training is safe and improves capacity and quality of life.
**What does needing three pillows to sleep suggest?** Orthopnoea from pulmonary congestion.
**A patient has gained 3 kg in 2 days. What do you do?** Postpone training and inform the medical team; possible fluid retention.
**What NYHA class is breathlessness on walking a short distance on the flat?** Class III.
**Why know the ICD threshold?** To keep exercise HR safely below it to avoid inappropriate shocks.
